test_title: PYST 50: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 04 Nov, 2024 - Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

A good lawyer / always looks in the / case before he / attends court.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase "**looks in the**" is grammatically incorrect in the given context.
 
• The correct phrasal verb is "**looks into the case**", which means to examine or investigate the case carefully.
 
• "Look in" refers to briefly visiting a place, which does not fit the meaning of a lawyer preparing for a case.
 
• Therefore, the error lies in **part 2** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"A good lawyer always looks into the case before he attends court."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1) attends court** – This is grammatically correct. "Attend court" is a common collocation in legal contexts.
 
• **3) case before he** – This phrase is contextually and grammatically accurate.
 
• **4) A good lawyer** – This phrase is correct and serves as the proper subject of the sentence.
